title: Five times four is twenty
rule: Treat 5×4=20 as a chord you already know, then scale zeros.
example: 50 × 40 is the same chord with two extra zeros → 2,000.

title: Build a hard fact from an easy one
rule: Do not memorize 7×8 as a unique island. 7×4=28, double → 56. Or 7×10−7×2.

title: Keep squares and powers of two
rule: Squares through 30 and 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 pull other tricks. Cubes to 10 help too.

title: Scale by tens by moving zeros
rule: ×10 appends a zero; ×100 appends two. Do not recompute the base fact.

title: Ignore decimal points, then put them back
rule: Multiply the digits as whole numbers. Count total places to the right of the points and park them at the end.

title: One percent is two places left
rule: 1% of a number is that number with the decimal moved two places left. 10% is one place.

title: Percents swap
rule: A% of B is the same as B% of A. Pick the easier half.

title: Tens of percent of tens
rule: Drop a zero from each side, multiply, and you already moved two decimal places.

title: Build percents from 50 / 25 / 10 / 5
rule: Half, quarter, tenth, and half of a tenth. Add the chunks you need.

title: Twelve and a half percent is divide by eight
Half a percent and two percent
rule: 1% is two places left. 2% is twice that. 0.5% is half of it.

title: Twenty percent is double then one place left
rule: ×2, then move the decimal one place left (that is ÷10).

title: Divide by five: double, then shift
rule: ×2, then move one place left.

title: Hourly to monthly is ×720
rule: 24 × 30 ≈ 720. Hourly cost × 720 ≈ monthly cost.

title: Monthly to daily is ÷30
rule: A month is about 30 days. Reverse: daily × 30 ≈ monthly.

title: Monthly to yearly is ×12
rule: Twelve months. Yearly to monthly is ÷12. ×12 is ×10 plus ×2.

title: Users needed is cost ÷ price
rule: Reduce both sides by tens first. 3,000 ÷ 50 → 300 ÷ 5 → 60.
example: Cost $3,000, price $50 → 60 users to break even.

title: Markup is price ÷ cost
rule: How many times cost is the price? Subtract 1× to hear the extra as a percent of cost.
example: $2 on $0.33 cost is about 6×, so roughly a 500% markup on cost.

title: Chain shortcuts in one breath
rule: Hourly ×720 → monthly. Monthly ÷ price → users per box. Track A math inside a Track B sentence.

title: Ceiling is price times possible customers
rule: Max revenue ≈ price × reachable customers. If infra already rivals that ceiling, the model is weak.
example: $20/mo × 10k users = $200k/mo. A $150k cost base is tight.

title: LTV should be about 3× CAC
rule: Revenue over life versus what you paid to acquire.

title: Runway is cash divided by burn
rule: Cash ÷ monthly burn. Directional, not a spreadsheet close.

title: Twenty percent a month is not a 50× year
example: 100 users cannot become 50,000 at 20% in a year (~900).

title: Add left to right
rule: Lock the large place first, then pour in the rest as a running total.

title: Round, then pay it back
rule: Round to an easy number, compute, then compensate with the opposite sign.

title: Estimate with compatible numbers first
rule: Before the exact payback, round both factors to something you can do instantly so the magnitude is locked.

title: Add 99 or 998 by overshooting
rule: Add the round number, then take back the gap. +99 is +100 −1; +998 is +1,000 −2.

title: Round a factor, subtract the extra copies
rule: Round one factor to a round number; the payback is (gap × other factor).

title: Times five is times ten, then half
rule: ×4 and ×8 are repeated doubles. ×25 is ×100 then ÷4.

title: Times fifty is times 100, then half
rule: ×50 = ×100 ÷ 2. ×75 is three-quarters of ×100.

title: Times 125 is times 1000, then ÷8
rule: 125 = 1000/8. Add three zeros, then halve three times.

title: Halve one side, double the other, drop even rows
rule: Russian peasant / Egyptian: keep doubling. Add the rows where the halved side was odd (binary bits).

title: Egyptian doubling ladder
rule: Double one factor into rungs (1×, 2×, 4×, 8×). Write the other factor as powers of two and add those rungs.

title: Near tens: ×9, ×11, n5 squared
rule: ×9 is ×10 minus the number. ×11 parks the digit sum in the middle. n5² is n(n+1) then glue 25.

title: Three-digit times eleven is neighbor sums
rule: Write the first digit, then each adjacent pair, then the last digit. Carry when a pair is 10 or more.

title: Times 99 is times 100 minus the number
rule: ×99 = ×100 − n. ×101 = ×100 + n. Same shape as ×9 / ×11 one place larger.

title: Times 101 parks the number beside itself
rule: ×101 = ×100 + n. For two digits that is ab0 + ab.

title: Square near 100 with (100±d)²
rule: 10000 ± 200d + d². Two middle digits from 2d, last two from d².

title: Common fractions are percents
rule: Memorize 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, 1/8, 1/10. Scale from there.

title: Sixths and ninths
rule: 1/6 ≈ 0.1667 (half of a third). 1/9 = 0.111…, and n/9 repeats n. 2/3 = 66⅔%.

title: Rule of 72
rule: Years to double ≈ 72 ÷ annual percent rate (compounding).

title: ARR is MRR times twelve
rule: ARR ≈ MRR × 12. One-time fees are not MRR.

title: Lifetime months ≈ 1 / monthly churn
rule: 5% monthly churn → about 20 months. Do not mix monthly with annual churn.

title: NRR is same-customer revenue later
rule: Ending revenue from a cohort ÷ starting revenue. Expansion can push it over 100%.
example: Start $100k, later $130k from those accounts → 130% NRR.

title: Rule of 40
rule: Growth % + margin % should land around 40 or better (later-stage smell test).

title: Burn multiple is burn over new ARR
rule: Net burn ÷ net new ARR. 1–2× is efficient; 5×+ is expensive growth.

title: Payback is CAC over monthly gross profit
rule: Aim for ≤12 months. Use profit after COGS, not list price.

title: Marketplace revenue is GMV times take
rule: Volume is not revenue. Multiply by the cut.

title: Card fees ≈ 2.9% plus 30 cents
rule: Small tickets are a much higher percent. For a smell test, about 3% of volume.

title: Fully loaded is salary times 1.3
rule: Benefits and tax are not free. Default load is ×1.3.

title: Percent sold is cash over post-money
rule: Post-money = pre-money + cash. Investor % ≈ cash / post.
example: Pre $8M, raise $2M → post $10M, sold 20%. Listen for pre vs post.

title: Fermi TAM is customers times yearly price
rule: Stack round numbers, then take a believable slice. Watch for a 10× error in one factor.

title: Twenty percent carries about eighty
rule: Take 20% of the count as the heavy slice; treat that slice as ~80% of load or revenue.

title: Revenue is price times users
rule: R = P × U. Any side from the other two: users = revenue ÷ price.

title: Three and nine are digit sums
rule: A number is divisible by 3 (or 9) when the digit sum is. Keep summing to a single digit for 9.

title: Four looks at the last two digits
rule: ÷4: last two. ÷8: last three. ÷2 last digit even. ÷5 ends 0 or 5. ÷25 ends 00, 25, 50, 75.

title: Eleven is the alternating sum
rule: Add / subtract digits in turn. 0 or a multiple of 11 (including negatives) means yes.

title: Seven, thirteen, seventeen, nineteen: trim the last digit
rule: Drop the last digit d. For 7 subtract 2d; for 13 add 4d; for 17 subtract 5d; for 19 add 2d. Repeat until you recognize the multiple.

title: Endings for 16, 20, 50, 125
rule: ÷16 looks at the last four digits. ÷20 ends 00/20/40/60/80. ÷50 ends 00/50. ÷125 has last three in 000, 125, 250 … 875.

title: Composite divisors are two coprime tests
Vertical, then crosswise, then vertical
rule: Ones product, then the two cross products added, then tens product. Carry as you go.

title: Three digits is five slots
rule: Each slot sums every digit pair whose places add to that slot. Middle slot has three products. Carry right to left.

title: Equally far from a center is a² − b²
rule: (c−d)(c+d)=c²−d². Find the midpoint, square it, subtract the gap squared.

title: Same tens digit, ones add to ten
rule: Left: tens × (tens+1). Right: ones product. Glue them.

title: Near-square pair around a known square
rule: 73 × 77 sits on 75: 75² − 2². Need a nearby square you already know.

title: Around a thousand
rule: Same identity, bigger center: (1000 − d)(1000 + d) = 1,000,000 − d².

title: Turn division into an easier multiply
rule: ÷5 is ×2 then ÷10. ÷25 is ×4 then ÷100. ÷4 / ÷8 are repeated halves. ÷0.5 is ×2.

title: Factor the divisor, or ask × what
rule: ÷12 = ÷3 then ÷4 (or the reverse). Or hear 12 × ? = 168.

title: Scale both until the divisor is whole
rule: Multiply dividend and divisor by the same 10s. Division does not change.

title: Partial quotients: overshoot, then back off
rule: Jump to a round multiple of the divisor, then add or remove single copies.

title: Division is a missing factor
rule: Ask “divisor × what = dividend?” and use the table fact you already know.

title: ÷20 and ÷0.125
rule: ÷20 is halve then one place left. ÷0.125 is ×8 (an eighth fits eight times in one).

title: Pair a long sum to tens
rule: In a list, grab pairs that make 10, 100, or 1,000, then count the pairs.

title: Pair the ends of a run
rule: 1+2+…+n = n(n+1)/2. Pair first with last; there are n/2 copies of (n+1).

title: Complements to five
rule: 4 = 5 − 1, 3 = 5 − 2. +4 becomes +5 then −1. The abacus habit before the ten-complement.

title: Any even run is count × average
rule: Sum of an evenly spaced run = number of terms × (first + last) / 2. Gauss is the 1…n case.

title: Add the same to both sides of a subtract
rule: a−b = (a+c)−(b+c). Push the subtrahend to a round 10 or 100.

title: Cancel factors before you multiply fractions
rule: Any numerator may cancel with any denominator. Multiply the thin leftovers.

title: Compare fractions by cross products
rule: a/b vs c/d: compare a×d and b×c. Larger product is the larger fraction.

title: Digit root checks a product modulo 9
rule: Sum digits until one remains. Factors’ roots times each other must match the answer’s root. A mismatch is definitely wrong.

title: Last digit of a product is last digits multiplied
rule: Only ones digits matter. If the claim ends in the wrong digit, stop.
example: 327×648 cannot end in 5 because 7×8=56 ends in 6.

title: Digit roots check sums too
rule: Root of the sum must equal the sum of the roots (reduced). Same filter as multiplication.

title: Nearby square, then bump d / 2a
rule: If N = a² + d, then √N ≈ a + d/(2a).

title: One Babylonian step: average the guess and N/guess
rule: x_new = (x + N/x) / 2. One pass is usually enough to smell-test.

title: Regroup a product so a pair becomes 10 or 100
rule: (a×b)×c = a×(b×c). Pair 25 with 4, 125 with 8, 5 with 2.

title: Do not multiply left to right out of habit
rule: Scan for a pair that makes a power of 10, then dump the leftover onto that.

title: Split one factor into easy pieces
rule: a × (b + c) = ab + ac. Break the friendlier factor by place or into round pieces.

title: Factor the multiplier
rule: Replace an awkward multiplier with factors and apply them one at a time: ×18 = ×9 then ×2.

title: Flip the product
rule: a × b = b × a. Read 17 × 6 as six 17s or seventeen 6s — whichever splits easier.

title: Only 10–20% are on at once
rule: Concurrent ≈ 10% (low) to 20% (busy) of logos. 100 users is not 100 simultaneous jobs.
example: 100 logos → about 10–20 active. Size infra for 20, not 100.

title: Boxes is users divided by per-box capacity
rule: Server count ≈ users ÷ users each box can hold. Cancel zeros first.

title: Revenue per box versus cost per box
rule: Price × users-on-that-box, then compare to the monthly box cost.
example: $30 × 20 users = $600 vs $720/mo box → losing $120 per server.

title: Plan at about 70% of max
rule: Safe load ≈ 0.7 × advertised capacity. Do not size as if you run at 100%.
example: 10 jobs/sec max → plan on 7. 100 seats → 70 filled.

title: Always add 30% to a cost guess
rule: Estimated cost × 1.3. Different story from salary ×1.3 (benefits): this is undercount pad.

title: SaaS funnel bands, then compress
rule: Visit→signup ~10–30%, signup→paid ~2–10%. Mid smell: 20% then 5%.

title: Round neighbors: one copy off
rule: ×9, ×19, ×99, ×999 are round minus one copy. ×11, ×101, ×1,001 are round plus one copy.

title: Small builds: ×3, ×6, ×12, ×15, ×18
rule: ×3 = double + original. ×6 = ×5 + original. ×12 = ×10 + ×2. ×15 = ×10 + half of it. ×18 = ×20 − ×2.

title: Fractions of a power of ten: ×20, ×25, ×50, ×75, ×125
Below the base: cross subtract, multiply the gaps
rule: Distances from 100 (or 1,000). Left = one number minus the other’s gap. Right = gap product with as many digits as the base has zeros.

title: Above, or one of each
rule: Above: cross add and glue the gap product. One above and one below: the gap product is negative, so subtract it.

title: Base 1,000 keeps three digits on the right
rule: Same moves; the right side is three digits wide.

title: (a + b)² and (a − b)²
rule: Square the round part, add or subtract twice the cross term, add the small square.

title: Same ones digit, tens add to 10
rule: Left: tens product + the ones digit. Right: ones digit squared, two places.

title: Ends in 5 for any size
rule: n5² → n × (n+1), then glue 25.

title: Place-value partial products
rule: Split one factor by place, multiply each part, add the big partial first.

title: Area grid: split both sides
rule: Every product is a rectangle. Split both factors by place, fill the cells, add.

title: Line and lattice are the same grid drawn
rule: Line multiplication counts crossings by diagonal; lattice adds cell digits by diagonal. Good for seeing, slow for big numbers.

title: Five-complement: +4 is +5 −1
rule: When the ones run out, add a five and take the complement back. +3 is +5 −2.

title: Squares 1–30
rule: Anchor 15², 20², 25², 30²; step to neighbors with (n+1)² = n² + n + (n+1).

title: Cubes to 10 and powers of two
